t: You're in Hyde Park, a 350-acre Royal Park divided by the Serpentine and the Long Water. It's part of a chain of green spaces running from Kensington Palace to St James's Park. The park is known as the site of the Hamilton–Mohun duel, in which the Duke of Hamilton and Lord Mohun both died. The quarrel was over a disputed inheritance. Hamilton had led opposition to the Act of Union in Scotland's parliament. The architect Decimus Burton, the writer Jane Welsh Carlyle and the cricketer A. G. Steel are also recorded as having died here.
